claim: Tubefilter reported Linktree's finding that the majority of creators who do secure brand deals are paid less than $100 per sponsored post, a stronger statement than TechCrunch's report of the same data, which said 12% of creators earn under $100 per collaboration.
stance_target: The precision of the Linktree brand-deal payment figures as they circulated through press coverage
scope_conditions: Linktree survey n≈9,500 fielded 2021; the underlying report PDF does not contain either formulation, so the two outlets read different online materials or interpreted the same chart differently
quoted_support: The majority of the surveyed creators have not engaged in any brand deals at all, and even among those who do, the majority take home less than $100 per paid post.
numbers: 70% earn <10% of income from brand deals

claim: Two-thirds of Linktree's surveyed creators self-identified as niche creators, and Tubefilter reported the niche earnings premium as only 2 percentage points more likely to earn six figures and 11 percentage points more likely to have posted branded content.
stance_target: The claim that niche specialization materially improves creator income outcomes
scope_conditions: Linktree survey n≈9,500 fielded 2021; cross-sectional and uncontrolled for tenure or audience size; the underlying absolute rates are 7% versus 5% for six-figure income and 37% versus 26% for branded content
quoted_support: the nouveau niche are 2% more likely to earn six figures per year, and they're 11% more likely to have posted at least one piece of branded content.

claim: Tubefilter independently confirms that more than a third of Linktree's surveyed creators had been making content for a year or less and that 59% of those beginners had not turned on monetization at all.
stance_target: The claim that a large share of the active creator population is in its first year and unmonetized
scope_conditions: Linktree survey n≈9,500 fielded 2021; corroborates TechCrunch's 36% figure for the under-one-year tenure bucket
quoted_support: More than a third of the creators Linktree analyzed have only been making content for a year or less, and among those "beginner creators," only 6% have made more than 10,000 from their work. 59% of them haven't turned on monetization at all.
numbers: more than a third under one year

claim: Tubefilter characterised Linktree's 200 million figure as people 'earning money from digital content creation', a materially stronger claim than Linktree's own definition, which requires only that a person produce and seek to monetize content.
stance_target: The claim that 200 million people earn money from content creation
scope_conditions: Headline framing versus Linktree's stated definition; Linktree's own survey found 53% of creators earned $100 or less annually, which is inconsistent with 200 million people meaningfully earning money
quoted_support: Linktree claims that the so-called creator economy — the global community of artists, thinkers, and doers who monetize their content on social media — now includes about 200 million moneymaking individuals.
